A newcomer who can already run a script would follow the story of the bug, but would trip on the JavaScript in the code boxes, on the unlabelled old code in the test step, and on words like pull request, diff and skills that this lesson uses without saying what they mean.

13-mcp-in-plain-words.html 7/10. A newcomer would grasp what MCP is quickly, but would struggle to actually set one up: where the app's settings file lives, what npx and Node.js need, and what the 'make it yours' task asks them to do.

13-mcp-in-plain-words.html 7/10. A newcomer would get the idea of MCP and its safety rules, but would get stuck on how to actually add a server to an app, because the lesson never says where the settings go.

13-mcp-in-plain-words.html 7/10. A newcomer would grasp the USB-C idea and the safety rules, but would get stuck on the setup: where the config goes, what npx and Node.js do, and why the tool list looks different from what they expect.

06-voice-agents.html 7/10, 14-context-and-sub-agents.html 8/10. A newcomer would struggle most with terms the lessons use before explaining them, such as the model and tools in the first lesson and the n8n sub-agent step in the second.
03-docs-and-email.html 6/10, 12-webhooks-and-sub-workflows.html 7/10.

07-agile-roles.html 7/10, 18-organisational-change.html 7/10, 19-closing-a-project.html 8/10. A newcomer would struggle most with terms used before they are explained, and with a model made for one person being applied to a whole team.

07-agile-roles.html 7/10, 18-organisational-change.html 8/10, 19-closing-a-project.html 7/10. A newcomer would struggle most with agile words used before they are explained, such as sprint, stand-up, increment and Scrum, and with the risk-or-issue question that a quiz tests without teaching.

03-choosing-an-approach.html 7/10, 04-leading-a-team.html 8/10, 17-compliance-and-governance.html 8/10. A newcomer would most often get stuck on project-management jargon the lessons use without a gloss, such as change control, product backlog, retrospective, business case and sponsor, rather than on anything technical.

05-products-and-services.html 8/10, 06-four-dimensions.html 7/10, 08-guiding-principles.html 8/10, 14-value-streams.html 7/10. A newcomer would struggle most where the four dimensions end and the outside factors (PESTLE) begin, since a supplier is both outside and a dimension, and with jargon the lessons use without explaining, such as API, triage and “agent”.
